bugs.creator: kevinushey
bugs.summary: Follow guidance from Unicode TR31 in determining valid identifiers for UTF-8 locales

comments.creator: kevinushey
comments.text:
Currently, when running in a MBCS locale, R allows for certain unicode strings as symbols -- for example,

> x <- list("你好" = 42)
> x$你好
[1] 42

However, this is not true for some other unicode strings; for example:

> x <- list("नमस्ते" = 42)
> x$नमस्ते
Error: unexpected input in "x$नमस्"

I believe this occurs because 'नमस्' contains nonspacing marks, as per

https://apps.timwhitlock.info/unicode/inspect?s=%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B8%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%87

And the R parser requires each individual character in a symbol name to be considered as alphanumeric (or '.' or '_'):

https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/8df226e3b2c140e48bfbbbe5157a459b7e9a213b/src/main/gram.c#L5364-L5367

This requirement is also checked in do_makenames (which replaces such characters with a '.'):

https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/8df226e3b2c140e48bfbbbe5157a459b7e9a213b/src/main/character.c#L1034

but may be checked in other places as well.

Could R expand what it considers to be a valid symbol name, to include strings composed of both letters and marks?

(Note: I use links to the GitHub mirror just because it makes it easy to browse the sources directly in a web browser; I understand they're not the canonical sources.)

---

> sessionInfo()
R version 4.1.2 (2021-11-01)
Platform: aarch64-apple-darwin20.6.0 (64-bit)
Running under: macOS Monterey 12.0.1

Matrix products: default
LAPACK: /opt/homebrew/Cellar/r/4.1.2/lib/R/lib/libRlapack.dylib

locale:
[1] en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8/C/en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8

comments.creator: kevinushey
comments.text:
To add some more color; the Unicode specification provides TR31 to describe recommended defaults for what unicode strings a programming language should consider to be valid identifiers:

https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr31/

In particular, the specification defines a set of unicode classes which can be considered as valid for the 'start' of a symbol, and what can 'continue' a symbol.

> ID_Start characters are derived from the Unicode General_Category of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, titlecase letters, modifier letters, other letters, letter numbers, plus Other_ID_Start, minus Pattern_Syntax and Pattern_White_Space code points.

> ID_Continue characters include ID_Start characters, plus characters having the Unicode General_Category of nonspacing marks, spacing combining marks, decimal number, connector punctuation, plus Other_ID_Continue , minus Pattern_Syntax and Pattern_White_Space code points.

Other programming languages, e.g. Python, appear to adhere to this specification:

https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/06c4ae8b1380eec1c5f3cd8faa21102d1c940bab/Objects/unicodeobject.c#L12323-L12358

Given the prior art in this space, I think it is reasonable for R to try and follow this specification as well.
